title: Santaguida 1995: csa fibre corrected of psoas major at L5-S1 (M, supine)

imaging.modality: MRI Philips Gyroscan 1.5 T, spin echo TR 500 TE 20
imaging.plane: transverse slices 10 mm apart T12-mid sacrum; values given at disc levels

quantity.name: csa_fibre_corrected
quantity.definition: anatomical CSA multiplied by cosine of fibre angle to the plane normal (authors may call it PCSA/physiological area; NOT volume/fibre-length PCSA); L5/S1 area corrected by cos 20 deg between slice and fibre line of action

source.sample: 15 males (MRI) + 7 male embalmed cadavers; MRI: young healthy men (same demographics as McGill 1993: 25.3 y, 176.1 cm, 81.5 kg; very likely the same subjects); cadavers for architecture

how_to_simulate: Pose the model supine (lying; lordosis as when lying, no gravity load on trunk).
Select all psoas major fascicles whose path crosses the plane at L5-S1 (transverse slices 10 mm apart T12-mid sacrum; values given at disc levels), one side.
Sum their PCSA; use PCSA directly (fibre-angle corrected area).
Compare the one-side total with the measured mean +/- SD (bilateral sums are labelled side=bilateral_sum).
protocol.notes: The "corrected CSA using Bogduk 1992" column (2107, 2406 mm2 at L4/L5, L5/S1) is a cumulative physiologic area computed from Bogduk 1992 fascicle data with an assumed 13.5 cm fibre length - model-derived, not stored. McGill 1993 Table 2 gives right/left psoas at the same levels for (very likely) the same subjects.
